WATCH DOGS 2

One of Ubisoft's best open-world games. You can hack almost anything in San Francisco, apart from the terrible driving physics.

RATINGS:
- Gameplay: 9/10
- Graphics: 8/10
- Open World: 9/10
- Hacking: 10/10
- Story: 7/10
- Driving: 5/10
- Replayability: 8/10

PROS:
+ San Francisco is genuinely fun to explore.
+ Hacking is brilliant. Messing with traffic lights, cars and random people's phones never gets boring.
+ Loads of freedom in how you complete missions.
+ Drones and RC cars make stealth missions really enjoyable.
+ The world feels alive, with NPCs actually doing things.
+ Great soundtrack and atmosphere.
+ Still looks surprisingly good for a 2016 game.
+ Police chases can be hilarious.

CONS:
- Driving feels awful, especially at high speeds.
- Enemy AI can be incredibly stupid.
- Some missions get repetitive.
- The story tries a bit too hard to be cool sometimes.
- Gun combat feels out of place in a game about hacking.
- Ubisoft somehow made every security guard willing to die protecting a server room.

VERDICT:

Watch Dogs 2 is genuinely underrated. The hacking mechanics are fantastic, the map is great and there's so much random stuff to mess around with.

You can spend 30 minutes carefully hacking cameras and distracting guards to complete a mission without being spotted, or accidentally run someone over and spend the next 20 minutes escaping the police.

My only real complaint is the driving and occasionally questionable AI.

FINAL SCORE: 8.5/10

Spent more time causing traffic accidents remotely than actually completing missions.

I like that you have some freedom to decide how you want to complete each mission instead of just one approach.

As for the story, hmm... it's not as complicated or dramatic as the first game, but honestly, I didn't expect it to be that serious anyway. This game is more about a group of young hackers going up against a big corporation, and I think the more comedic way works pretty well. The dialogue is one of my favorite parts because each character have a lot of personality, and their conversations is funny af.

I also really enjoy the side quests. Some of them are surprisingly entertaining, and there are plenty of funny moments if you take the time to explore the world. One of the funniest things is how you can invade people's privacy and discover some weird shit about them.

Overall, yeah, I'd say this is a pretty good game. The missions might get repetitive after a while, and the story isn't too deep but the enjoyable gameplay, funny dialogue and freedom to approach missions in different ways. It's not a game I'd play expecting an emotional story, but if you just wanna mess around in an open world as a hacker this one does the job pretty well.

I utterly adore this game, and I believe the developers took a giant step forward from the first Watch Dogs (which is already great in my opinion). The addition of a difficulty selector solved the problem of Aiden's immortality of the previous game; the realistic difficulty made the game tougher and more challenging. I loved the game's vibe, the parkour animations, the San Francisco map, all the characters, the references to Watch Dogs 1, and just driving around with no real destination. Even without the free Ultra Texture Pack DLC and with my PC's specs, I found the graphics amazing.

One small detail I really appreciated is that the city feels alive, and not just like a background for the player. NPCs interact with each other, park their vehicles, try to steal parked cars, and so on. 

It's a pity that there are only a few players online and that servers aren't very stable. Related to this, there's the issue of getting the Showd0wn achievement since it takes a lot of time to find players if you don't do it with friends.

Regarding the critical aspects, I encountered a few game crashes and freezes, which were kinda frustrating, though I believe they were caused by stressing my computer too much. I also found a couple of bugs and glitches throughout the game, honestly though, not as many as ppl complain about. Moreover, in my opinion, both drones are too powerful; unlocking the ability to drop explosives and electroshocks from them partly kills the gameplay by making it simpler. 

As in any Ubisoft game, there might be some issues when playing it for the first time, and that could require some time to fix, but in the end I think it's worth putting the head on. The discounted price is a real bargain for what this game offers.
